nodes.title: Finite-coefficient model of completed homology
nodes.statement: Fix the tame level K^p, a compact open K_0 of the p-adic group with a countable basis of open normal subgroups U, and the neat finite-type tower Y_U with the finite free O-local system of CC.3/completed-homology-and-borel-moore. For every n the coefficient-reduction maps induce an O[[K_0]]-linear homeomorphism H̃_n ≅ lim_s H̃_{n,s}, where H̃_{n,s} = lim_U H_n(Y_U, O/varpi^s); likewise H̃_n^{BM} ≅ lim_s lim_U H_n^{BM}(Y_U, O/varpi^s). The isomorphisms commute with the support map H̃_n → H̃_n^{BM}, covering pushforward, conjugation and the transported tame Hecke maps. Consequently the rational completed homology of Fu, (lim_s lim_U H_n(Y_U, Z/p^s)) ⊗_{Z_p} K for a finite extension K/Q_p, is K ⊗_{Z_p} H̃_n for O = Z_p: rationalisation is applied after both limits. It is not the limit lim_U H_n(Y_U, E) of rational finite-level homology: in the tower of connected degree-p covers of a circle the first is 0 and the second is E.
hypotheses: O is the ring of integers of a finite extension E of Q_p, with uniformizer varpi and finite residue field k.

Fixed tame level K^p; every Y_U is a neat finite level with the finite cellular model of ALS.1/finite-complex-model (relative cells of the Borel–Serre pair for Borel–Moore homology), so its homology with coefficients in a finite O-module is a finite O-module.
The coefficient system is the finite free O-local system fixed in CC.3/completed-homology-and-borel-moore; for an algebraic lattice W_0 the integral local actions are those of H_int = Stab_H(W_0).
Fu's instance: O = Z_p and the rationalisation is ⊗_{Z_p} K for a finite extension K of Q_p.
proofSteps: At a fixed level U the cellular chain complex C_U is a bounded complex of finite free O-modules (ALS.1/finite-complex-model), and H_n(Y_U, O/varpi^s) = H_n(C_U/varpi^s) is a finite O-module; for Borel–Moore homology use the relative complex of the Borel–Serre pair.

For fixed n the systems s ↦ Z_n(C_U/varpi^s) and s ↦ B_n(C_U/varpi^s) consist of finite modules, so they are Mittag-Leffler and their lim¹ vanishes (ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.1/mittag-leffler-lim-one). So lim_s is exact on 0 → B_n → Z_n → H_n → 0 and on 0 → Z_n → C_n → B_{n−1} → 0, and lim_s H_n(C_U/varpi^s) = H_n(lim_s C_U/varpi^s) = H_n(C_U) since C_U is varpi-adically complete.

Coefficient reduction commutes with covering pushforward, so (U, s) ↦ H_n(Y_U, O/varpi^s) is a functor on a product of two directed sets and its limit may be taken in either order: lim_s lim_U H_n(Y_U, O/varpi^s) ≅ lim_U lim_s H_n(Y_U, O/varpi^s) = lim_U H_n(Y_U, O) = H̃_n.

Both sides are compact Hausdorff, being limits of finite discrete modules, and the comparison is a continuous bijection, hence a homeomorphism. Deck transformations, supports and the transported Hecke correspondences commute with coefficient reduction, so the map is O[[K_0]]-linear for the action of CC.3/iwasawa-action-on-homology.

Rationalisation: K ⊗_{Z_p} (−) is applied to the integral limit. In the tower of connected degree-p covers of a circle, pushforward on H_1(−, O) = O is multiplication by p, so H̃_1 = 0, whereas lim(E ← E ← …) along multiplication by p is E because p is invertible in E.
acceptance: Circle tower of connected degree-p covers: H̃_{1,s} = lim(O/varpi^s ← O/varpi^s ← …) along multiplication by p is 0 for every s, H̃_1 = 0, and the comparison is the zero isomorphism.
Zero-dimensional regular tower Y_U = K_0/U: H̃_{0,s} = (O/varpi^s)[[K_0]] and its limit over s is O[[K_0]] = H̃_0, the test regular_zero_homology of CC.3/completed-homology-and-borel-moore.
Non-example for commuting limits with rationalisation: in the circle tower E ⊗_O H̃_1 = 0 while lim_U H_1(Y_U, E) = E.

At s = 1 the composite H̃_n ≅ lim_s H̃_{n,s} → H̃_{n,k} is the reduction map of the Bockstein sequence of CC.3/finite-coefficient-duality-and-bockstein, with cokernel H̃_{n−1}[varpi]; in the circle tower H̃_{0,k} = k and H̃_0 = O, consistent with H̃_{−1} = 0.

uses.how: The finitely generated torsion Iwasawa module and the descent spectral sequence (38) are stated for this rational double-limit model; CC.5/semisimple-homology-torsion and CC.6/homological-hyperTor-descent prove them for H̃_n, and this comparison transports them.
The fixed-exponent modules H̃_{n,s} are the ones that duality pairs with the fixed-exponent cohomology; this node says how they assemble to H̃_n.

sources.match: Fu defines completed homology at a fixed tame level as the limit over the exponent s of the limit over p-levels of homology with Z/p^s coefficients, tensored afterwards with a finite extension K of Q_p, and quotes its finite generation over K[[G]] from Emerton and Calegari–Emerton.

Calegari and Emerton define completed homology as the limit over the tower of homology with Z_p coefficients, assuming each space has the homotopy type of a finite simplicial complex so that all these groups are finitely generated, and state that the projective-limit topology is the canonical one.

nodes.title: Completed modules at varying tame level
nodes.statement: Let Σ₀ be a finite set of finite places of F not above p, G_{Σ₀} = ∏_{v∈Σ₀} G(F_v), and fix the level K^Σ at the finite places outside Σ = Σ₀ ∪ {places above p}. For a compact open K_{Σ₀} ⊂ G_{Σ₀} with K_{Σ₀}K^Σ neat, write H̃^n_c(K_{Σ₀}) for the completed compact-support cohomology (CC.2, support c) and H̃_n^{BM}(K_{Σ₀}) for the completed Borel–Moore homology (CC.3) of the p-tower at tame level K_{Σ₀}K^Σ. For K'_{Σ₀} ⊂ K_{Σ₀}, finite-cover pullback gives res: H̃^n_c(K_{Σ₀}) → H̃^n_c(K'_{Σ₀}) and the finite-cover transfer gives tr: H̃_n^{BM}(K_{Σ₀}) → H̃_n^{BM}(K'_{Σ₀}); both commute with the p-level and coefficient transitions. Define H̃^n_{c,Σ} = colim_{K_{Σ₀}} H̃^n_c(K_{Σ₀}) along res and H̃_{n,Σ}^{BM} = colim_{K_{Σ₀}} H̃_n^{BM}(K_{Σ₀}) along tr. Conjugation of tame levels gives each a smooth O-linear action of G_{Σ₀}, commuting with the action of the p-adic group at each tame level and with the tame Hecke operators at places outside Σ. The colimit is taken after completion in s; it is a different construction from the fixed-exponent tame colimit of CC.1/tame-level-variation, and the two are not identified here.
hypotheses: O is the ring of integers of a finite extension E of Q_p, with uniformizer varpi and finite residue field k.
Σ₀ is finite and contains no place above p; K^Σ is fixed; every tame level K_{Σ₀}K^Σ used is neat.

For K'_{Σ₀} normal in K_{Σ₀}, the cover at level K'_{Σ₀}K^Σ over level K_{Σ₀}K^Σ is a finite Galois cover whose group is the effective quotient of K_{Σ₀}/K'_{Σ₀}; its degree divides [K_{Σ₀} : K'_{Σ₀}]. For Shimura quotients with infinite central units the effective deck group is verified under gap G12.
The invariants statement requires K_{Σ₀} of pro-order invertible in O (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.0:abelian-category/unit-pro-order).
proofSteps: At each p-level and exponent, pullback and finite-cover transfer between tame levels are the ALS pullback and the finite-cover transfer of the AlgebraicTopology supplier; they commute with p-level pushforward and pullback and with coefficient reduction, so they pass to the completed modules of CC.2/coefficient-limit-completion and CC.3/completed-homology-and-borel-moore.

Form the two filtered colimits in O-modules. Conjugation by g ∈ G_{Σ₀} carries level K_{Σ₀} to gK_{Σ₀}g⁻¹ and commutes with res and tr, so G_{Σ₀} acts; a class coming from level K_{Σ₀} is fixed by K_{Σ₀}, so the action is smooth (SR.0:abelian-category/smooth-rep-category).

For K' normal in K of index invertible in O: cor∘res is multiplication by the degree and res∘cor is the group sum over the deck group (CC.1/restriction-corestriction-normalisation, applied at every exponent and passed to the limit). Hence res is injective with image the invariants, and the averaging projector e_K of SR.0 satisfies e_K∘ι_{K'} = ι_K∘[K : K']⁻¹ cor; the finite form of this identity is Tau Ceti's Representation.averageMap_eq_invOf_card_smul_norm. The Borel–Moore side is the same with tr and pushforward exchanged.
Invariants commute with filtered colimits of smooth modules when e_K exists, which gives (H̃^n_{c,Σ})^{K} = H̃^n_c(K) and the Borel–Moore analogue.
acceptance: An element in the image of level K_{Σ₀} is fixed by every g ∈ K_{Σ₀}: conjugation by g maps level K_{Σ₀} to itself and acts there as the identity.
For a finite group acting with invertible order, the averaging identity of TameCompleted.averaging_comp_ι is Tau Ceti's Representation.averageMap_eq_invOf_card_smul_norm (averageMap = ⅟|G| • norm).
Pushforward after transfer is multiplication by the degree on the Borel–Moore side, and cor after res is multiplication by the degree on the cohomology side, at every exponent and after completion.

uses.how: The completed Borel–Moore homology of modular curves at tame level Σ₀ is the colimit of the fixed-tame-level modules along restriction, with its smooth action of G_{Σ₀}; restriction there is the Poincaré dual of the transfer used here.
The compactly supported completed cohomology at tame level Σ₀ has K_{Σ₀}-invariants equal to the fixed-level module, and the projector restricted to a smaller level is the normalised trace.
Both colimits, the invariants identification and the projector formula are the inputs of the tame-level duality.
The residual-localised Borel–Moore module at tame level Σ₀ is built from this colimit.

api.name: TameCompleted.ι
api.statement: Structure maps H̃^n_c(K_{Σ₀}) → H̃^n_{c,Σ} and H̃_n^{BM}(K_{Σ₀}) → H̃_{n,Σ}^{BM}, compatible with res and tr respectively.

api.name: TameCompleted.exists_ι
api.statement: Every element of either colimit is ι_K x for some open K_{Σ₀} inside a fixed compact open K⁰_{Σ₀}, and ι_K x = ι_K y exactly when x and y agree after res (respectively tr) to some open K′ ⊂ K; the open subgroups of K⁰_{Σ₀} are cofinal, so restricting to them gives the same colimit.

api.name: TameCompleted.desc
api.statement: A family of O-linear maps f_K : H̃^n_c(K_{Σ₀}) → W with f_{K′} ∘ res = f_K for K′ ⊂ K induces a unique O-linear map H̃^n_{c,Σ} → W with desc ∘ ι_K = f_K, and likewise along tr on the Borel–Moore side; it is G_{Σ₀}-equivariant when W is a G_{Σ₀}-module and g ∘ f_K = f_{gKg⁻¹} ∘ g for the conjugation maps.

api.name: TameCompleted.smooth
api.statement: Every element of either colimit is fixed by a compact open subgroup of G_{Σ₀}; an element in the image of level K_{Σ₀} is fixed by K_{Σ₀}.

api.name: TameCompleted.invariants
api.statement: For K_{Σ₀} of pro-order invertible in O, ι identifies H̃^n_c(K_{Σ₀}) with (H̃^n_{c,Σ})^{K_{Σ₀}} and H̃_n^{BM}(K_{Σ₀}) with (H̃_{n,Σ}^{BM})^{K_{Σ₀}}; in particular ι is injective.

api.name: TameCompleted.averaging_comp_ι
api.statement: For K' ⊂ K of index invertible in O, e_K ∘ ι_{K'} = ι_K ∘ [K : K']⁻¹ cor on H̃^n_c(K'), with e_K the averaging projector of SR.0.

api.name: TameCompleted.equivariant
api.statement: The G_{Σ₀}-action commutes with the action of the p-adic group at each tame level and with tame Hecke operators at places outside Σ.

api.name: TameCompleted.of_empty
api.statement: For Σ₀ = ∅ the structure maps are isomorphisms from the fixed-level modules.

tests.name: tameCompleted_empty
tests.statement: With Σ₀ empty, H̃^n_{c,Σ} = H̃^n_c(K^p) and H̃_{n,Σ}^{BM} = H̃_n^{BM}(K^p).

tests.name: tameCompleted_points
tests.statement: For levels Y(K) = K⁰/K of a profinite K⁰ of pro-order invertible in O with trivial p-tower, H̃^0_{c,Σ} = C^∞(K⁰, O) with translation action, and its K-invariants are the functions on K⁰/K; H̃_{0,Σ}^{BM} = colim_K O[K⁰/K] along the maps sending a coset to the sum of the smaller cosets it contains.

tests.name: tameCompleted_p_index
tests.statement: For the connected degree-p cover of a circle, pullback on H^1(−, F_p) = F_p is zero; with a p-power index the transition is not injective and level invariants are not recovered.

tests.name: tameCompleted_transfer_not_pushforward
tests.statement: For the connected double cover of a circle with p odd, transfer H_1(S^1, O) → H_1(S^1, O) is an isomorphism and pushforward after transfer is multiplication by 2; the Borel–Moore colimit uses transfer, not pushforward.

sources.match: The completed Borel–Moore homology at tame level Σ₀ is defined as the direct limit over compact opens of G_{Σ₀} of the fixed-level modules along restriction maps, and carries a smooth action of G_{Σ₀}.

For a compact open of pro-order prime to p, the projector onto invariants is defined with the normalised Haar measure; the invariants of the tame-level compactly supported completed cohomology are the fixed-level module, and the projector restricted to a smaller level is the corestriction divided by the index.

nodes.title: Tame-level Borel–Moore duality
nodes.statement: In the setting of CC.3/tame-level-completed-modules, fix a compact open K⁰_{Σ₀} ⊂ G_{Σ₀} of pro-order invertible in O, the O-valued Haar measure μ on G_{Σ₀} with μ(K⁰_{Σ₀}) = 1, and a degree n. Suppose that H̃^{n+1}_c(K_{Σ₀})[varpi^∞] = 0 for every open K_{Σ₀} ⊂ K⁰_{Σ₀}, so that by the compact-support and Borel–Moore case of CC.3/duality-between-completed-homology-and-completed-cohomology the evaluation map h_{K_{Σ₀}}: H̃_n^{BM}(K_{Σ₀}) → Hom_O(H̃^n_c(K_{Σ₀}), O) is a homeomorphism of compact O-modules. Put V = H̃^n_{c,Σ}. Then the maps μ(K_{Σ₀})·h_{K_{Σ₀}}, followed by the identification Hom_O(V^{K_{Σ₀}}, O) ≅ (Ṽ)^{K_{Σ₀}}, λ ↦ λ∘e_{K_{Σ₀}}, of SR.0, are compatible with the transfer transitions, and induce an O-linear isomorphism H̃_{n,Σ}^{BM} ≅ Ṽ onto the smooth contragredient of V. It restricts at each K_{Σ₀} to a homeomorphism H̃_n^{BM}(K_{Σ₀}) ≅ (Ṽ)^{K_{Σ₀}}, and it is equivariant for G_{Σ₀}, for the p-adic group with the contragredient convention of CC.3/continuous-dual-conventions, and for each tame Hecke correspondence at places outside Σ, which acts on Borel–Moore homology by the transposed correspondence. Without the torsion hypothesis h_{K_{Σ₀}} has kernel Hom_O(H̃^{n+1}_c(K_{Σ₀})[varpi^∞], E/O) and no isomorphism is asserted.
hypotheses: O is the ring of integers of a finite extension E of Q_p, with uniformizer varpi and finite residue field k.
The hypotheses of CC.3/tame-level-completed-modules, with K⁰_{Σ₀}K^Σ neat; for GL₂ one may take K⁰_{Σ₀} = ∏_{l∈Σ₀}(1 + l M₂(Z_l)), which is pro-l at each l ∈ Σ₀.
G_{Σ₀} is unimodular (a product of groups of points of reductive groups), so μ(gKg⁻¹) = μ(K).

H̃^{n+1}_c(K_{Σ₀})[varpi^∞] = 0 for all open K_{Σ₀} ⊂ K⁰_{Σ₀}. For modular curves and n = 1 this holds because the completed H^2_c vanishes, the result of Emerton that Nakamura cites in the proof of his Lemma 2.4.
proofSteps: Fixed tame level: the compact-support and Borel–Moore case of the integral duality CC.3/duality-between-completed-homology-and-completed-cohomology gives 0 → Hom_O(H̃^{n+1}_c[varpi^∞], E/O) → H̃_n^{BM} → Hom_O(H̃^n_c, O) → 0. Under the hypothesis h_K is a continuous bijection of compact Hausdorff modules, hence a homeomorphism (Nakamura, Lemma 2.4, for the modular curve).

Transitions: for K' ⊂ K ⊂ K⁰, transfer on Borel–Moore homology is adjoint under evaluation to the trace (corestriction) on compact-support cohomology: both are the finite-cover transfer of the AlgebraicTopology Stage 5 supplier on relative chains of the Borel–Serre pair, with the adjointness requested from that stage, and ALS.3/level-trace identifies that trace with the level trace. With e_K∘ι_{K'} = ι_K∘[K : K']⁻¹ cor (TameCompleted.averaging_comp_ι) and μ(K') = [K : K']⁻¹ μ(K), the square formed by μ(K)h_K, λ ↦ λ∘e_K, transfer and μ(K')h_{K'} commutes. This is Nakamura's second diagram in §2.3.2, whose lower row lands in Hom_O(Ĥ¹_c(K'_{Σ₀}), O) (correcting a misprint in the printed diagram).

SR.0 smooth-dual (3) identifies Hom_O(V^K, O) with (Ṽ)^K for K of pro-order invertible in O, and TameCompleted.invariants gives V^K = H̃^n_c(K); these identifications are compatible with the inclusions (Ṽ)^K ⊂ (Ṽ)^{K'}.
Pass to the colimit over the cofinal family of open K ⊂ K⁰: every vector of Ṽ is fixed by some such K, so the union of the (Ṽ)^K is Ṽ, and the colimit of H̃_n^{BM}(K) along transfer is H̃_{n,Σ}^{BM}.

Equivariance: conjugation by g carries μ(K)h_K to μ(gKg⁻¹)h_{gKg⁻¹} because μ is conjugation invariant; the p-adic group acts through the contragredient convention; a Hecke correspondence acts on homology by its transpose, for which evaluation is invariant (CC.1/tame-hecke-on-colimits). In Nakamura's cohomological model of H̃_1^{BM} through Poincaré duality this transposed action is T'_l = T_l S_l⁻¹, S'_l = S_l⁻¹.
acceptance: Zero-dimensional example of CC.3/tame-level-completed-modules: the isomorphism sends the coset gK to the functional f ↦ ∫_{gK} f dμ on C^∞(K⁰, O). Without the factor μ(K) the maps fail to commute with transfer by the factor [K : K'].

Modular curves, n = 1: the isomorphism is Nakamura's identification of H̃_{1,Σ}^{BM} with the smooth contragredient of Ĥ¹_{c,Σ}; its Galois equivariance uses the Galois action transported by CC.8/transported-arithmetic-actions. Nakamura writes Ĥ¹_c, the varpi-adic completion of the integral level colimit; here it is the H̃¹_c of this node, because every finite-level H²_c(Y_K, O) is torsion-free, so the Tate-module term of CC.2/the-four-completed-modules-and-the-p-adic-completion-versus-tate-module-splitting vanishes.
If H̃^{n+1}_c(K)[varpi^∞] ≠ 0, the kernel Hom_O(H̃^{n+1}_c(K)[varpi^∞], E/O) of h_K is nonzero.
With K⁰ = GL₂(Z_l) and p dividing |GL₂(F_l)| the normalisation μ(K) is not defined in O; first pass to a pro-l open subgroup.

sources.match: At a fixed tame level the evaluation map from completed Borel–Moore homology to the O-dual of compactly supported completed cohomology is a topological isomorphism, because the Calegari–Emerton sequence has a torsion term that vanishes since the completed H^2_c is zero.
Hecke operators on the Borel–Moore side are normalised as T'_l = T_l S_l⁻¹ and S'_l = S_l⁻¹ so that the duality map is Hecke-linear.

With a compact open of pro-order prime to p and the normalised Haar measure, the normalised fixed-level duality maps composed with the projector identification assemble into a Hecke- and group-equivariant topological isomorphism from the tame-level Borel–Moore homology to the smooth contragredient of the tame-level compactly supported completed cohomology.

nodes.title: Control of complete torsion-free complexes
nodes.statement: Let M^• be a bounded-above complex of varpi-adically complete, varpi-torsion-free O-modules. Then (1) no nonzero element of H^i(M^•) has a compatible system of varpi-power roots (x_0 = x and varpi x_n = x_{n−1}): Hom_O(E, H^i(M^•)) = 0, hence its varpi-adic Tate module lim_n H^i(M^•)[varpi^n] (transitions multiplication by varpi) is zero. This does not say that H^i(M^•) has no nonzero varpi-divisible element (one lying in varpi^n H^i(M^•) for every n); without the hypothesis of (4) such elements can exist; (2) for every n there is a natural exact sequence 0 → H^i(M^•)/varpi^n → H^i(M^•/varpi^n) → H^{i+1}(M^•)[varpi^n] → 0, and these sequences form an inverse system whose third terms have transition multiplication by varpi; (3) the induced map lim_n H^i(M^•)/varpi^n → lim_n H^i(M^•/varpi^n) is an isomorphism; (4) if moreover lim_n H^i(M^•/varpi^n) has bounded varpi-power torsion for every i, then H^i(M^•) → lim_n H^i(M^•)/varpi^n is also an isomorphism, so H^i(M^•) is varpi-adically complete and separated and equals lim_n H^i(M^•/varpi^n). The statement is for complete and torsion-free terms: for M = E in degree 0 the limit of H^0(M/varpi^n) is 0 while H^0(M) = E.
hypotheses: O is the ring of integers of a finite extension E of Q_p, with uniformizer varpi and finite residue field k.
M^• is bounded above; each M^i is varpi-adically complete and separated (IsAdicComplete for the ideal (varpi)) and varpi-torsion-free.
Clause (4) also assumes that every lim_n H^i(M^•/varpi^n) has bounded varpi-power torsion.
proofSteps: Divisible elements: if x_n ∈ H^i(M) satisfy varpi x_n = x_{n−1} with x_0 ≠ 0, lift them to cocycles x̃_n and choose y_n with d y_n = x̃_{n−1} − varpi x̃_n; the convergent sum y = Σ varpi^{n−1} y_n satisfies dy = x̃_0, a contradiction. So Hom_O(E, H^i) = 0, and the Tate module, a submodule of Hom_O(E, H^i) by the sequence 0 → O → E → E/O → 0, vanishes.

Bockstein: M is varpi-torsion-free, so 0 → M → M → M/varpi^n → 0 (multiplication by varpi^n) is exact; its long exact sequence gives (2), and comparing n + 1 with n shows that the transition on the third terms is multiplication by varpi.

The third terms form a system with zero limit by (1). The first terms H^i/varpi^n have surjective transitions, so their lim¹ vanishes (ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.1/mittag-leffler-lim-one) and the limit of the exact sequences gives (3).

Completeness: H^i(M) is a quotient of the complete module of cocycles, so H^i(M) → lim H^i(M)/varpi^n is onto. If its kernel K were nonzero, bounded torsion (varpi^k kills the torsion of the limit) shows varpi K = K, which with (1) forces K = 0.
acceptance: M = O in degree 0: both limits are O.

M = [O → O] in degrees 0, 1 with differential multiplication by varpi: H^0 = 0 and H^1 = O/varpi = k. H^0(M/varpi^n) = varpi^{n−1}O/varpi^n ≅ k is nonzero for every n, and the Bockstein sequence identifies it with H^1[varpi^n] = k, whose transitions are multiplication by varpi, hence zero: the limit of the H^0(M/varpi^n) is 0 = H^0(M).
Completeness is needed: M = E in degree 0 is torsion-free but not complete, and E is varpi-divisible with lim_n E/varpi^n = 0 ≠ E.

Divisible elements need not vanish without the hypothesis of (4): let M^0 = M^1 be the varpi-adic completion of the free O-module on e_1, e_2, … (the null sequences in O) and d(e_n) = varpi^n e_n. The class of w = Σ varpi^n e_n in H^1 is nonzero, since a preimage would have to be Σ e_n, which is not a null sequence, yet w − d(e_1 + … + e_{k−1}) lies in varpi^k M^1 for every k, so the class lies in every varpi^k H^1. Here lim_m H^1/varpi^m is the completion of the direct sum of the O/varpi^n, whose varpi-power torsion is unbounded, and Hom_O(E, H^1) = 0 still holds.

uses.how: Pan's bounded-torsion inverse-limit argument for A_inf-coefficient cohomology of the perfectoid modular curve applies this lemma to a Čech complex; the request to CC.2 asks for exactly this control.
Identifies the completed tensor form of completed cohomology with arbitrary complete torsion-free coefficients.

sources.locator: §4.4, Lemma 4.4.4, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e7, statement p. 44, proof p. 45 (arXiv:2008.07099v3, p. 48)
sources.match: For a bounded-above complex of p-adically complete p-torsion-free modules whose mod-p^n cohomologies have limits with bounded torsion, cohomology is the limit of its reductions and the limit of the mod-p^n cohomologies; the proof shows that no cohomology module receives a nonzero map from Q_p, uses the universal-coefficient sequence with multiplication by p on the torsion terms, and concludes by a divisibility argument.

nodes.title: Integral cochain model and completed coefficients
nodes.statement: For the lifted finite-cell tower of CC.4 at fixed tame level, let S̃^• be its integral admissible cochain model, the termwise continuous O-dual of the completed chain complex 𝒫 (CC.4/perfectness-and-cochain-comparison). Then S̃^• is a bounded complex of varpi-adically complete, varpi-torsion-free O-modules, with natural isomorphisms H^i(S̃) ≅ H̃^i and H^i(S̃/varpi^m) ≅ A^i_m, where A^i_m = colim_U H^i(Y_U, O/varpi^m), compatible with tower transitions, the integral local action and the transported Hecke maps; the same holds for the compact-support and boundary models. For every varpi-adically complete, varpi-torsion-free O-module M, with trivial action on the tower, the completed cohomology with coefficients M, H̃^i(M) = lim_m colim_U H^i(Y_U, M/varpi^m), is naturally isomorphic to lim_m (A^i_m ⊗_O M). If the varpi-power torsion of H̃^{i+1} is bounded, as CC.5/bounded-integral-torsion proves for this tower, H̃^i(M) is moreover the varpi-adic completion of H̃^i ⊗_O M.
hypotheses: O is the ring of integers of a finite extension E of Q_p, with uniformizer varpi and finite residue field k.
The hypotheses of CC.4/completed-equivariant-cell-complex and CC.4/perfectness-and-cochain-comparison: a lifted finite-cell regular tower over a compact p-adic analytic K_0, at fixed tame level.

M is varpi-adically complete, separated and varpi-torsion-free, and the tower acts trivially on it; any further action on M (for example a Galois action on A_inf-type coefficients) is carried along by naturality.
The completed-tensor clause assumes that varpi^c kills the varpi-power torsion of H̃^{i+1} for some c.
proofSteps: Terms: 𝒫_i = Λ^{c_i d}, so S̃^i = Hom_cont,O(𝒫_i, O) = C(K_0, O)^{c_i d}, varpi-adically complete and torsion-free (finite projective summands in the descended model).

Reductions: continuous maps into the discrete O/varpi^m factor through finite levels, so S̃/varpi^m = colim_U Hom_O(𝒫 ⊗_Λ (O/varpi^m)[K_0/U], O/varpi^m) = colim_U C^•(Z_U, O/varpi^m) by CC.4/derived-finite-level-coinvariants (underived, as 𝒫 is finite projective); exactness of filtered colimits (CC.1/fixed-exponent-smooth-colimit) gives H^i(S̃/varpi^m) ≅ A^i_m.
Integral cohomology: CC.2/integral-admissible-complex-control gives H^i(S̃) ≅ lim_m H^i(S̃/varpi^m) = H̃^i, naturally for the transitions and actions of CC.4/perfectness-and-cochain-comparison.

Coefficients: M/varpi^m is flat over O/varpi^m because M is torsion-free, so colim_U C^•(Z_U, M/varpi^m) = (S̃/varpi^m) ⊗_{O/varpi^m} M/varpi^m and its cohomology is A^i_m ⊗_O M; take the limit over m.

Completed tensor: tensoring the Bockstein sequences of CC.2/complete-torsion-free-complex-control for S̃ with the flat M/varpi^m gives 0 → (H̃^i ⊗ M)/varpi^m → A^i_m ⊗ M → H̃^{i+1}[varpi^m] ⊗ M → 0. With varpi^c killing the torsion, c consecutive transitions of the third terms vanish, so their limit and lim¹ are zero and the limit of the middle terms is the completion of H̃^i ⊗_O M.
acceptance: M = O: the coefficient formula is lim_m A^i_m = H̃^i, the definition in CC.2/coefficient-limit-completion.

M = O[[T]] (complete and torsion-free, not finitely generated over O): H̃^i(O[[T]]) = lim_m (A^i_m ⊗_O O[[T]]) is the submodule of H̃^i[[T]] of the series Σ_j a_j T^j such that, for every m, the images of the a_j in A^i_m generate a finitely generated O-module; it is not H̃^i[[T]] in general. In the zero-dimensional tower Y_U = K_0/U with K_0 = Z_p, H̃^0(M) = C(Z_p, M) for the varpi-adic topology of M, and Σ_j 1_{p^j Z_p} T^j lies in C(Z_p, O)[[T]] = H̃^0[[T]] but not in H̃^0(O[[T]]): the indicator functions are linearly independent in A^0_1 = C^∞(Z_p, k).
Circle tower of connected degree-p covers: A^0_m = O/varpi^m and A^1_m = 0 (pullback is multiplication by p on H^1), so H̃^0(M) = M and H̃^1(M) = 0 for every complete torsion-free M.

uses.how: Pan's identification of completed cohomology with A_inf/(ker θ)^k coefficients is the case M = A_inf/(ker θ)^k of the coefficient formula; the request to CC.4 asks for this complex and this interchange.

uses.where: Pan, On locally analytic vectors II, Lemma 7.2.6, arXiv v1 p. 120
uses.how: The stronger form for every p-adically complete torsion-free coefficient module.

sources.locator: §7.2, Lemma 7.2.6(1) and its proof, arXiv:2209.06366v1, p. 120
sources.match: Completed cohomology with coefficients in a p-adically complete torsion-free module is the limit over m of the mod-p^m completed cohomology tensored with the module; the proof uses a complex of complete torsion-free modules computing completed cohomology and its reductions (attributed to Emerton), the universal-coefficient sequences and multiplication by p on the torsion terms.

targetCoverage.target: Indexing category of levels, with cofinal normal and pro-p sequences
targetCoverage.comparison: Compact opens of the p-adic group ordered by inclusion, with labelled conjugation arrows and their composition law. A countable normal basis is taken inside a fixed compact open, and it can be chosen pro-p after passing to an open uniform subgroup, which NoncommutativeAndEquivariantIwasawa:NE.0 supplies (RT-AREA-automorphic-1/3).

targetCoverage.target: Finite covering correspondences, their composition identities and the conjugation maps
targetCoverage.comparison: One diagram of ordinary, compact-support and boundary complexes with pullback in the level and reduction in the exponent; trace is a separate reverse system. Identity and composition laws, compatibility with reduction, supports and tame Hecke operators. Same-lattice integral conjugation is restricted to H_int.

targetCoverage.target: Levels with stabilisers: the stack or derived group-cohomology model, with torsion retained
targetCoverage.comparison: The ALS groupoid or derived group-cohomology model at a non-neat level, descent from a neat normal refinement by RΓ(Q, −) including Q-torsion. A neat cofinal tower does not remove the stabilisers of a fixed non-neat level.

targetCoverage.target: Compact support through compatible compactifications or the j! model, with trace maps
targetCoverage.comparison: Topologically, compact support is the ALS Borel–Serre model with proper pullback and trace. For Shimura varieties the j! model of a proper algebraic compactification is compared with it, naturally in finite étale level maps, together with the unnormalised trace and the orientation dictionary.

targetCoverage.target: Singular, cellular and étale finite-coefficient models compared under exact hypotheses
targetCoverage.comparison: Étale–Betti comparison for finite locally constant coefficients on neat characteristic-zero Shimura varieties, with compact support; the cellular–singular comparison is part of the lifted cellular tower of CC.4. Constructible-coefficient and compactification-independence proofs are the owner's gap G10.

targetCoverage.target: Acceptance tests on actual towers
targetCoverage.comparison: Neat modular curves through ModularCurvesPartII:R14.3 and an anisotropic compact quotient: pullback, trace (trace after pullback is the degree), conjugation, supports and the cusp incidence diagram.

targetCoverage.target: Filtered colimit at fixed exponent, in modules and in complexes; independence of cofinal restriction; exactness
targetCoverage.comparison: A^n_{*,s} = colim_K H^n(C^*_{K,s}) for the three supports, the colimit of complexes, and the exact-colimit identification of their cohomology; cofinal restriction through the final-functor comparison.

targetCoverage.target: Action of the local group by conjugating levels; open stabilisers; smoothness
targetCoverage.comparison: Left action through the CC.0 conjugation dictionary; every class has an open stabiliser, so the action is smooth. For a fixed algebraic lattice only H_int acts integrally.

targetCoverage.target: Commuting tame Hecke operators from double correspondences, with explicit normalisation
